main_answer_reason: The report substantively distinguishes the trial and High Court findings, marriage evidence, competing provenance, customary-law limits, and withheld outcome. It nevertheless misidentifies the case in its caption, misses several distinct evidence and defense positions, omits possession relief, generalizes benamidar status, and adds unsupported claims concerning Hindu-law testamentary capacity and marriage as the sole determinant of priority.
